civilopediaText.text: A Civil War ruleset for Unciv, beginning with the Battle of Gettysburg, July 1-3, in the third summer of the war.

New Game > Map Type: Scenario > 'Battle of Gettysburg'. The scenario sets the ruleset, map and both armies for you. The variants marked Easiest, Easier, Harder and Hardest are the same battle with a weaker or stronger AI army. You command the Union by default: to play the Confederacy, click the Human/AI button next to each army to swap them.

Or: Map Type: Custom > 'Gettysburg (free play)' for a free-form game on the historical terrain: no armies, cities or war at the start - you build your own army. In that mode, declare war on the enemy yourself on turn 1 (Diplomacy, top left).

One hex is about 250 yards. One turn is about one hour of daylight; each night is two turns. Turn 0 is 7 AM on July 1 and turn 47 is 7 PM on July 3. In the scenario, the top bar shows the day of July (the calendar) and the hour on the 24-hour clock (the watch) next to the turn number.

Units are brigades (infantry and cavalry) and battalions or brigades of artillery. The Confederate divisions that reached the field on July 1 start on the map. The Union starts with only Buford's cavalry and Wadsworth's division: its corps race up their roads hour by hour, as they did that day. All later reinforcements arrive on their historical roads at their historical times - open the 'Arrivals' buildings in the Civilopedia to see the timetables.

Each army's first turn opens with a briefing and its orders. At the great moments of the battle, a message tells what happened at that hour in the real battle. You can turn the history messages off from any of them; the reminder before the last turn always shows.
The armies are at war from the first turn. The terrain is revealed, but enemy troops are only seen where your own units can see them. Cities cannot be razed, and no new units can be raised.

Hold the Field: seven key positions - cities on Oak Hill, the Lutheran Seminary, Gettysburg, Cemetery Hill, Culp's Hill, the Angle and Little Round Top. At the end of turn 47 (nightfall, July 3), the side holding more of them wins.

Oak Hill, the Seminary and the Angle start in Union hands. The town, Cemetery Hill, Culp's Hill and Little Round Top start NEUTRAL (held by Adams County): both armies are at war with it and must take them by force - an empty position falls to a brigade or two. Until then they count for neither side.
Decisive Victory: capture the enemy army's headquarters at any time.

Rifle-muskets made frontal attacks against steady troops costly: use woods, stone walls, breastworks and high ground. Attack from several sides at once - every extra adjacent unit adds a flanking bonus. Artillery must unlimber (Set Up) to fire and needs line of sight, so put it on hills. Generals inspire troops within range, but a general who is caught falls.
